notes: Process assertions P1-P7 are shared across every eval: they encode the pipeline the skill exists to reproduce (cheap parallel researchers, per-claim sources, retained synthesis, funded blind verifier, cost disclosed first). The O-series assertions are per-eval and check the produced bundle. Running a full eval end-to-end costs roughly 0.6-1.1M tokens, so prefer the bounded conformance harness in ../../liang-replica-forge-workspace/ for routine regression checks and reserve full runs for real deliverables.
shared_process_assertions: P1 fan-out: 4 or more researchers are dispatched, one per slice, concurrently on Tier A (sequentially on Tier B, but with the identical schema and source discipline).
P2 cheap researchers: researchers are explicitly assigned a cheap/fast model (Haiku-class), never the session's top model.
P3 blind verifier funded: a blind, no-web buildability verifier runs at the strongest available model and high reasoning effort, and is never cut to save cost.
P4 fidelity pair: two web-enabled fidelity verifiers run on a mid-tier model with different, concretely enumerated focus areas.
P5 per-claim sources: each individual research finding carries the URLs actually consulted for that claim, not just a bibliography, and the research/ files preserve them.
P6 synthesis retained: prompt.md is authored by the orchestrator in main context, never delegated to a subagent.
P7 cost disclosed first: the expected token cost and the scale-down levers are stated to the user before the research phase spends anything.

evals.prompt: use liang-replica-forge: i want a replication benchmark prompt for the game Downwell (Moppin / Ojiro Fumoto, 2015). keep it cheap: 4 research slices, verify cap 1 round. faithful style (its 3-color palette IS the identity). single html file. i'll paste the result into different models to compare them.
evals.expected_output: A bundle at .liang/prompts/<slug>/ with: prompt.md carrying an anonymized codename, PART 0-3 structure, a physics table with derived gating math, the 3-color palette encoded as rules, and embedded verifier tables whose criteria all reference spec-defined systems; research/ files with per-claim source URLs; verification/round-1.md; README.md with declared deviations. The words Downwell, Moppin, Fumoto, and gunboots must not appear in prompt.md.
assertions: O1 anonymized: the strings Downwell, Moppin, Fumoto, Devolver, and gunboots appear nowhere in prompt.md (case-insensitive).
O2 structure: prompt.md contains all four parts — rules of engagement, mission, specification, and the embedded build-verify protocol.
O3 derived gating math: the spec states movement/physics numbers AND shows at least one derivation tying them to level geometry, so the mandatory route is provably traversable.
O4 style as rules: the restricted palette is given as explicit hex values with usage rules, not described in prose as a vibe.
O5 criteria are satisfiable: every row of every embedded verifier criteria table references only systems the specification actually defines, with matching numbers.
O6 cost instruction honored: exactly 4 research slices were run and verification stopped at 1 round, as the user asked.
O7 sources preserved: research/ contains one file per slice, each finding carrying at least one specific source URL.
O8 deviations declared: README.md lists the intentional differences from the real game, marked not to be 'fixed'.

evals.prompt: make me a replication prompt for Trello to benchmark models on. it's obviously too famous to hide so do whatever your skill says about that case. one core workflow slice: boards, lists, cards, drag and drop.
evals.expected_output: Software-domain bundle: object model specified before UI, workflows as precondition/steps/resulting-state, exact seeded demo data, the fidelity-vs-generic-clone-drift reframing declared in README, verifier roster swapped per domain-software.md (no audio verifier), local-only collaboration handling declared as deviation.
assertions: O1 drift reframing: because the target is unhideable, the README reframes the benchmark as fidelity-to-spec versus generic-clone drift instead of pretending anonymization works.
O2 drift punished in criteria: at least one verifier criterion explicitly penalizes drifting to a generic version of the product rather than following the spec.
O3 object model first: entities, fields, relationships and lifecycle states are specified before any UI layout.
O4 workflows are executable: each core workflow is written as precondition, numbered steps, and resulting state.
O5 seeded data: exact demo/seed content is specified, sufficient to exercise every specified behavior.
O6 roster swapped: the verifier roster matches the software domain — no audio verifier, and a data/behavior verifier is present.
O7 collaboration scoped: multi-user/real-time collaboration is explicitly scoped out and declared as a deviation rather than silently dropped.

evals.prompt: replica-forge this: SUPERHOT as a 3d browser game benchmark. time only moves when you move; white void, red enemies, black weapons. pick the medium knob yourself and justify it.
evals.expected_output: 3D-domain bundle: medium decision documented in PART 0 and README (likely one vendored lib), a camera section with numbers, a spatial beat map with landmark navigation, the style encoded as rules, scope held to 2-4 minutes per domain-3d-games.md.
assertions: O1 medium decided and justified: the vendored-library versus vanilla-WebGL choice is made explicitly, justified, and recorded in both PART 0 and the README.
O2 zero network preserved: whatever medium is chosen still runs with no runtime network requests.
O3 camera is first-class: a dedicated camera section gives follow distance/height/lag numbers, collision policy, pitch limits, and FOV baseline plus event kicks.
O4 spatial beat map: beats are described as connected spaces with landmarks, approximate dimensions, height deltas and sightlines, and the navigation rule is stated explicitly.
O5 geometry-cheap style: the look is encoded as palette plus material/shading rules implementable with procedural primitives, since the tested model ships no asset files.
O6 scope held: the slice targets roughly 2-4 minutes of play — one connected space chain, one skill ramp, one arena climax.
O7 time-mechanic specified numerically: the core time-moves-when-you-move rule is given as concrete time-scale values and the inputs that advance it.
